questions.learningObjective: Identify the binding constraint in a telescope budget
questions.stem: An amateur astronomer has 800 dollars and must choose between a 600 dollar mount and a 500 dollar camera

questions.explanation: Scarcity means limited resources against unlimited wants, so a choice is required. The mount alone fits but leaves no room for the camera, so both cannot be bought.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Describe what a production possibilities frontier means for an astronomer choosing between deep-sky photos and planetary photos

answer.exemplar: A production possibilities frontier shows the maximum combinations of deep-sky and planetary photos an astronomer can produce with fixed time and equipment, so points on it are efficient and points inside are wasteful.

questions.explanation: The frontier marks efficient use of fixed resources; inside points waste resources and outside points are unattainable. This frames tradeoffs between two outputs.

questions.explanation: Growth equals (44 minus 40) divided by 40 times 100, which is 10 percent. The base year output anchors the rate.

questions.explanation: A tradeoff arises when a fixed resource serves two competing ends. The cost of one choice is the other output given up.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: An investment of 600 dollars yields 120 dollars per year; how many years to recover the cost
questions.explanation: Payback equals 600 divided by 120, which is 5 years. The payback period measures how long investment takes to return.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A log notes 2 hours of darkness and 9 desired exposures

options.text: No scarcity exists because exposures are free
Exposures are scarce relative to dark time
Dark time is scarce relative to exposures
Scarcity applies only to equipment

questions.explanation: Limited dark time relative to desired exposures is scarcity. Scarcity applies to any limited resource, including time.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: A log chooses a 350 dollar filter over a 300 dollar eyepiece with 350 dollars total

options.text: The opportunity cost is 50 dollars saved
The opportunity cost of the filter is 350 dollars
options.misconception: uses price of chosen item as cost

options.text: The opportunity cost of the eyepiece is the filter
The opportunity cost of the filter is the eyepiece

questions.explanation: Choosing the filter means giving up the eyepiece. Opportunity cost is the forgone alternative, not money spent.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Explain why the production possibilities frontier is concave to the origin

answer.exemplar: The frontier is concave because increasing opportunity cost means each extra unit of one good costs more of the other as production shifts.

questions.explanation: Increasing opportunity cost produces a concave frontier. Equal costs would make it a straight line.

questions.subject: MACROECONOMICS
questions.stem: Output rose from 120 photos to 156 photos; what is the percentage growth
questions.explanation: Growth equals (156 minus 120) divided by 120 times 100, which is 30 percent. The base year anchors the rate.
